# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

items.t: Farmer ID (Kisan Pehchaan Patra) — AgriStack Farmer Registry
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Digital Agriculture Mission), with state Revenue and Agriculture departments

A free, lifelong 11-digit Farmer ID for every land-owning farmer, linked to Aadhaar and to the plots in the state's land records. Schemes such as PM-Kisan, crop insurance and Kisan Credit Card can then read your land details from the ID, so you stop carrying land papers for each one. New PM-Kisan applicants in the ten states that started first (UP, MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Assam) have needed a Farmer ID since 1 January 2025, and over 10 crore farmers had one by August 2026. You register once, at a village camp, a CSC or yourself on your state's Farmer Registry website.
Free lifelong Farmer ID, needed for new PM-Kisan registration and used for crop insurance and KCC
Any farmer who owns farm land recorded in the state's land records in his or her own name
Each owner of jointly held land registers separately. Land in several villages or states still gets one single Farmer ID
The name on Aadhaar must closely match the name in the land record. A big mismatch sends the claim for manual check or rejection
If the owner has died or the land was bought, the mutation (name transfer) must be done in the land record first
Tenant farmers and sharecroppers do not get the land in their name, but the owner can authorise them for a scheme
No fee is charged for registration or for the ID
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar for the OTP (otherwise fingerprint or face check at a camp or CSC)
Copy of the land record (khatauni, 7/12, jamabandi, RTC, patta or pahani) showing district, tehsil, village and survey / khasra number
Khata or owner number, for land held jointly
Mutation order or heirship entry, if the land came to you by inheritance or purchase

A Farmer Registry camp in your village (run by the Patwari / Lekhpal / Talathi, the agriculture assistant or a Krishi Sakhi), the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC), or the tehsil or block agriculture office. Take your Aadhaar, the mobile phone linked to it and a copy of your land record with the survey numbers; there is no paper form to fill. You can also register yourself online on your state's Farmer Registry site, whose address is the state code followed by fr.agristack.gov.in, for example upfr.agristack.gov.in (Uttar Pradesh), mhfr.agristack.gov.in (Maharashtra), gjfr.agristack.gov.in (Gujarat), rjfr.agristack.gov.in (Rajasthan), mpfr.agristack.gov.in (Madhya Pradesh) and bhfr.agristack.gov.in (Bihar).
Your own Aadhaar. The OTP for e-KYC goes to the mobile linked with it.
The enrolment number and the Farmer ID come by SMS to this number.

Go to a Farmer Registry camp or a CSC, or open your state's Farmer Registry site (state code + fr.agristack.gov.in), choose Farmer and create an account with your Aadhaar OTP.
Finish Aadhaar e-KYC. Your name and details come from Aadhaar; add your mobile number and address.
Plots already matched to your Aadhaar appear by themselves. For a missing plot, enter the district, sub-district, village and survey number, pick your name from the owners list and press Verify.
Give consent with an Aadhaar e-sign and submit. An enrolment number arrives by SMS.
The Patwari or revenue officer checks the claim against the land record. Once it is approved, the Farmer ID is made against your Aadhaar, usually within a day; check the status on the same site.
Quote the Farmer ID for PM-Kisan, crop insurance and KCC. If the claim is rejected for a name mismatch or a pending mutation, get the land record or Aadhaar corrected and claim again.

Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, with RBI, NABARD and banks

A cheap farm loan account with a RuPay card, given by banks to farmers for seeds, fertiliser, labour and other farming costs, and also for dairy, poultry, goat rearing and fish farming. Interest is 7% a year, and if you repay on time the government cuts it to 4% on loans up to Rs.3 lakh. No security is needed up to Rs.2 lakh. VB-G RAM G Rural Work Guarantee (Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card)
Ministry of Rural Development — Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025

From 1 July 2026 the VB-G RAM G Act replaced MGNREGA, and the old job card is becoming the Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card. Every rural household can now ask for up to 125 days of unskilled manual work a year, up from 100, paid at the notified wage into the worker's bank or post office account. An old MGNREGA job card with e-KYC done stays valid until the new card is issued; a household with no card registers free at the Gram Panchayat. Work must be given within 15 days of asking, or an unemployment allowance is due.
125 days of guaranteed wage work per household each year (up from 100 under MGNREGA), paid at the notified wage into the worker's bank or post office account
One card per household, listing all the adult members who want work; an old MGNREGA job card with e-KYC done stays valid until the new card comes
Single women, persons with disability, people over 60, freed bonded labourers, PVTG members and transgender persons get a Special card of a different colour
States can pause works for up to 60 days a year in peak sowing and harvest time; the 125 days are given in the rest of the year
Aadhaar cards of all the adult members to be listed — used for e-KYC and face-based attendance at the worksite
Passport-size photographs of those adult members, which go on the card
The old MGNREGA job card, if the household has one
All four, because work is given within 5 km of the village named here as far as possible — if it is further away, inside the Block, you are owed an extra 10 per cent of the wage.
One against each name in the same order. Aadhaar is used for e-KYC and face-based attendance, and wages are paid through Aadhaar-based payment, so a missing number holds up that member's wages.
Asked for identification only. The scheme has no poverty condition — a household above the poverty line is equally entitled to a card.
The photographs go on the card itself, next to each listed member's name.
Ask for this dated receipt. It is the proof that fixes the 15-day deadline for issuing the card.

If your household already has an MGNREGA job card, ask the Gram Rozgar Sevak whether e-KYC is done for every adult on it. Such a card stays valid until the new Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card is issued, so you do not need to apply again.

A household with no card applies at the Gram Panchayat: any adult member gives the names, ages and address of the household — orally, on plain paper or on the printed form free at the Panchayat. List every adult who might ever want work.

Attach Aadhaar copies, the residence proof, the bank passbook copy and one photograph of each listed adult, and take a dated receipt with a registration number. The Panchayat must issue the card within 15 days, and it is valid for three years.

Getting the card is not the same as asking for work. Ask for at least six days of work — orally, in writing on Form 6, or through the digital system — at the Gram Panchayat or to the Programme Officer, and take a dated receipt.

Work must start within 15 days, as far as possible within 5 km of your village. If it does not, the State owes you an unemployment allowance of at least a quarter of the wage for the first 30 days and half after that.

Attendance at the worksite is taken by face authentication. Wages are paid weekly, or at the latest within 15 days of the muster roll closing, straight into your account; after that you are owed 0.05% of the unpaid wage for each day of delay.

Check your days and payments on the card, on the Janata Board at the worksite and on vbgramg.dord.gov.in. Never let the Sarpanch, the Rozgar Sevak or anyone else keep your card. For a complaint, go to the Programme Officer at the Block, then the District Programme Coordinator (the Collector).

No national toll-free number. Complain to the Programme Officer at the Block office, then the District Programme Coordinator (Collector), or call your state's rural employment helpline; online complaints at pgportal.gov.in
Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (Rs.1,000 a month for TB patients)
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare — Central TB Division, National TB Elimination Programme

Every person being treated for tuberculosis (TB) gets Rs.1,000 a month for food for the whole length of treatment, usually Rs.6,000 for a six-month course, paid straight into a bank account. It covers treatment at a government hospital or by a private doctor, as long as the TB case is notified on the government's Ni-kshay system. Underweight patients also get extra nutrition supplements for the first two months, and families can get food baskets from Ni-kshay Mitra volunteers.

Paid for every month of treatment until the treatment ends
A child, or a patient without a bank account, can be paid into a parent's or guardian's account
Patients with a BMI below 18.5 also get energy-dense nutrition supplements for the first two months

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G Rural House)
Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development

Money to build a pucca house for a village family that has no house or lives in a kutcha one: Rs.1.20 lakh in the plains and Rs.1.30 lakh in hill states, the North-East and difficult areas, paid into the bank account in instalments as the house goes up. On top of that the family gets 90 days of paid labour (95 in hilly areas) on its own house under the rural job scheme, and Rs.12,000 for a toilet. Families are picked from the SECC 2011 list and the new Awaas+ 2024 survey and checked by the Gram Sabha; homeless and destitute families, manual scavengers, primitive tribal groups and freed bonded labourers come first. The scheme runs till March 2029 for 2 crore more houses.

Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana (formerly IGNDPS)
Ministry of Rural Development — Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly NSAP)

A monthly pension for persons with severe disability who belong to a below-poverty-line household. It was called the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) until the Union Cabinet renamed it on 14 October 2026, as part of the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly NSAP). The Cabinet also approved Rs.375 a month (Rs.625 from age 80), a 40 per cent disability limit instead of 80, and no minimum age; these start once the new guidelines are issued, due by mid-January 2027. Until then the old rules apply — age 18 or more and a certificate showing 80 per cent or more — and the state adds its own top-up.
Rs.300/month (Rs.500 after age 80) from the Centre, plus the state top-up; rising to Rs.375 (Rs.625 after age 80) once the new guidelines are issued
Age 18 years or more on the date of application (no minimum age once the new guidelines are issued)
Severe or multiple disability of 80 per cent or more, certified by the competent medical authority (40 per cent or more once the new guidelines are issued)
Disability certificate showing 80 per cent or more (40 per cent once the new guidelines are issued), issued by the Chief Medical Officer or a district medical board
Under the current rules you must be 18 or above. Once the new guidelines are issued, there is no minimum age.
Under the current rules it must read 80 per cent or more, or the Block office refuses it. Once the new guidelines are issued (due by mid-January 2027), 40 per cent or more qualifies.
